title: Addition of Vectors — Same and Opposite Directions
notes: Vectors are added by the head-to-tail rule. Place the tail of the second vector on the head of the first. The resultant runs from the tail of the first to the head of the second.
When two vectors point the same way along one line, the triangle collapses into a longer line. The magnitude of the resultant is R = P + Q, and the direction is that common direction.
When they point in opposite directions, the head-to-tail path folds back. The magnitude is R = |P − Q|, and the resultant points in the direction of the vector with the larger magnitude.
The general parallelogram result R = sqrt(P^2 + Q^2 + 2PQ cosθ) contains both cases. θ = 0° gives cosθ = 1 and R = P + Q. θ = 180° gives cosθ = −1 and R = |P − Q|.
A negative sign on a one-dimensional vector means the opposite direction. Subtracting is the same operation as adding the opposite vector.
The resultant of two equal opposite vectors is zero. The body they act on is then in translational equilibrium if no other force is present.

The resultant is therefore 7 N east.
